Struggle deeply — disrespect eats at me and I find it hard to move on until it is addressed

questions.question: In a season of waiting — when the outcome is uncertain and you cannot control what happens next — you are most likely to:

options.text: Prepare spiritually and strategically, then act with courage when the moment arrives
Stay faithful to my principles and trust that deliverance will come, even if I cannot see how
Draw close to my community and seek strength in shared prayer and support
Distract myself and hope things work out — I do not handle uncertainty well
Take matters into my own hands — waiting feels like weakness and I prefer action

questions.question: When it comes to using your position or influence for others' benefit, your honest assessment is:

options.text: I am willing to use my platform for others, even at great personal cost
I am better at seeing others' potential and calling them into it than stepping forward myself
I contribute most effectively as part of a team rather than as the leader or face of a cause
I have influence but I do not always use it wisely — I can be swayed by persuasive people
I use my influence to advance my own goals — I have worked hard for my position and I intend to protect it

questions.question: When you think about God's role in your daily life, the statement that resonates most is:

options.text: I believe I am where I am for a reason, and I am willing to act on that belief even when it is scary
I am deeply convinced that God is working behind the scenes, even when I cannot see evidence of it
I find God most present in community — in shared prayer, mourning, and celebration with others
I believe in God, but I do not always pause to consider how He might be directing my decisions
I rely more on my own plans and abilities than on any unseen divine purpose

results.title: You Are Like Esther — The Courageous Advocate
results.description: Like Esther, you possess a rare combination of inner strength and outward grace. You are willing to step into uncomfortable situations for the sake of others, and you understand that your position in life may serve a purpose far beyond your own comfort. You prepare carefully before acting, and when you move, you move with conviction. Your courage is not reckless — it is rooted in purpose and spiritual preparation. Esther's defining moment was not becoming queen; it was deciding to risk the crown for the sake of her people. You are at your best when you use your influence not for self-preservation but for sacrificial advocacy.
strengths: Willingness to sacrifice personal comfort for a greater cause
Strategic thinking combined with spiritual depth
Grace under pressure that wins favor with others
Ability to act decisively after careful preparation
watchFor: The temptation to stay silent when God is calling you to speak
Using your position for comfort rather than purpose
Waiting so long to act that the moment passes
Hiding your true identity or convictions out of fear rather than strategy

scripture.text: And who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?

results.title: You Are Like Mordecai — The Principled Mentor
results.description: Like Mordecai, you are a person of deep conviction who refuses to compromise on core principles, even when compliance would be easier and safer. You see the bigger picture — the purposes of God unfolding in the lives of people around you — and you are willing to challenge others into their calling. You are a mentor, a watchman, and a strategist. You may not always be the one in the spotlight, but your influence shapes the people who are. Mordecai refused to bow, challenged Esther to act, and trusted God's sovereignty even when facing annihilation. Your faith is active, principled, and contagious.
strengths: Unshakeable conviction in the face of pressure to conform
Ability to see others' potential and call them into it
Deep trust in God's providence, even without visible evidence
Strategic positioning that creates maximum influence
watchFor: Principled defiance that does not count the cost to others
Directing from the sidelines when God may be calling you to step forward
Expecting others to take the risks you identify but are not positioned to take
Rigidity that mistakes stubbornness for faithfulness

scripture.text: For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance for the Jews will arise from another place, but you and your father's family will perish.

results.title: You Are Like Haman — A Warning About Unchecked Ambition
results.description: This result is not a condemnation — it is a warning given in love. Like Haman, you may be driven by a deep need for recognition and control. You are ambitious, capable, and strategic, but these gifts become dangerous when fueled by pride rather than purpose. Haman had everything — wealth, power, family, royal favor — and none of it satisfied him because one man would not bow. If you find that your peace is held hostage by others' opinions, that slights consume your thoughts, or that your plans are driven more by personal vindication than by genuine service, this is your moment to change course. Haman's story does not have to be yours. Repentance and humility can redirect ambition from destruction to redemption.
strengths: Drive and ambition that achieve significant results
Strategic intelligence and political awareness
Ability to plan boldly and execute decisively
Natural leadership presence that commands attention
watchFor: Allowing personal slights to consume your peace and drive your decisions
Pursuing recognition so aggressively that it becomes an idol
Building 'gallows' for others that may become your own undoing
Mistaking the absence of opposition for genuine respect or loyalty

scripture.text: Pride goes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.

results.title: You Are Like Xerxes — The Influential Person Seeking Wisdom
results.description: Like Xerxes, you may occupy a position of significant influence without always recognizing the weight of your decisions or the quality of the voices you listen to. You are capable of great generosity and genuine affection, but you can also be swayed by the last person who speaks to you, making decisions without sufficient reflection. Xerxes was not evil — he was careless with his power. He authorized genocide because he did not bother to ask questions. He reversed course because Esther opened his eyes. Your story can go either way. The key is to surround yourself with Esthers, not Hamans — with truth-tellers who will challenge you, not flatterers who will manipulate you.
strengths: Position of genuine influence and authority
Capacity for generosity and affection
Ability to act decisively once truth is revealed
Willingness to reverse course when shown you are wrong
watchFor: Making significant decisions without asking sufficient questions
Being influenced by the last persuasive voice rather than the wisest one
Using power impulsively rather than reflectively
Delegating moral responsibility to others rather than owning your choices

scripture.text: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.

results.title: You Are Like the Jewish Community — The Faithful Collective
results.description: Like the Jewish people in Esther's time, your strength lies not in individual heroism but in community, solidarity, and shared faith. You find God most powerfully in the fellowship of others — in corporate prayer, in communal mourning, in shared celebration. You may not be the one standing before the king, but your fasting and prayers sustain the one who does. You understand that deliverance is a team effort and that behind every Esther stands a community that held her up. Your faithfulness in the background is not second-class faith — it is the foundation on which visible courage is built.
strengths: Deep commitment to community and mutual support
Faithfulness in prayer, fasting, and spiritual disciplines
Resilient identity that endures under pressure
Joy in celebrating God's faithfulness and passing the story to future generations
watchFor: Passivity that waits for others to act when God may be calling you personally
Using community as a hiding place to avoid individual responsibility
Fear-driven conformity that sacrifices distinctiveness for safety
Forgetting to celebrate and remember past deliverances, leading to discouragement in present trials

scripture.text: As the time when the Jews got relief from their enemies, and as the month when their sorrow was turned into joy and their mourning into a day of celebration.
